Review your notes and write a summary and reflection on the major points that we covered in class about the first act from Shakespeare's Macbeth.

Requirements: (out of 15 points)

1. (5pts) Summarize what has happened in Act 1

2. (4pts) Elaborate on 4 points that we covered in class.
3. (1pt) Include one compound sentence.

4. (1pt) Include one complex sentence.

5. (4pts) Use proper grammar and spelling. Write your reflection below adhering to the instructions above.

Act 1 of MacBeth begins with three witches entering with lightning and thunder.  They discuss where to meet MacBeth.  They decide to do so after the battle is done.  The witches make a famous statement, saying "foul is fair, and fair is foul."  Then, the witches disappear.  The king enters with a wounded captain.  The king stated that this bloody man helped set me free.  MacBeth and Banquo enter after their victory.  The witches appear to them, however; they don't look like women.  In fact, they don't look human at all!  They prophesy that MacBeth will become a noble of Cawdor and become king.  They told Banquo that he would not be king, but his children would be.  Eventually, Ross (a king's messanger) comes and calls MacBeth the thane of Cawdor.  MacBeth is confused, realizing that the witches cannot be bad, but also cannot be good.  MacBeth is now thinking about murder and is lost in thought.  The seed of ambition has been clearly planted.  Banquo notices MacBeth is uneasy.  He warns MacBeth not to trust the witches, suggesting that evil forces tell small truths to lure people into greater harm.  The king says that the Thane of Cawdor has been murdered.  Malcom is declared heir to the throne, blocking MacBeth's path to the throne.  The king plans to visit MacBeth's castle.  Lady MacBeth is reading a letter about the witches.  She plots to kill the king.  The king enters, saying the castle has a pleasant atmosphere.  MacBeth is afraid to kill the king, and Lady MacBeth calls him a coward.  MacBeth finally agrees to kill him.  Although Macbeth begins the play as a brave and loyal warrior, his ambition ultimately leads him to betray King Duncan and destroy his own sense of honor.  

In class, we elaborated on many points of Act 1.  We mainly focused on the witches attitudes and appearances.  First, the witches speak in Trochaic Tetrameter, instead of Iambic Pentameter (the main language used).  Next, we described the witches as inhuman and manly.  Lastly, the witches made the famous statment: "foul is fair and fair is foul" is symbolizing the reverse of expectations.  The fourth point we talked about was in relation to Lady MacBeth.  She is perceived as the man of the house, as she greets the king at the door, calls her husband a coward, and comes up with the plan of murder.

Act 1 of Macbeth began with the end of a battle. The king arrives at an encampment and inquires about the state of the ongoing war, and he discovers that one of his generals, Macbeth, alongside Banquo, had won the last battle and paved the way to victory. Before this happened, three witches were meeting to discuss when and where they should meet Macbeth. They decided to appear to Macbeth and Banquo after their battle and disappeared, saying fair is foul and foul is fair. Then they met Macbeth and Banquo and prophesied that Macbeth would be Thane of Cawdor and King and that Banquo would be the father of a king. Macbeth was troubled, but he was also tantalized by his ambition. He proceeded until servants approached him and told him that the king had made him Thane of Cawdor in place of a newly executed traitor. Afterwards,Macbeth and Banquo met the king and spoke and the king praised Macbeth greatly. The king decided to visit Macbeth's castle to honor Macbeth's loyalty. At the same time Lady Macbeth received a letter from Macbeth about the witches and what they foretold. She became rapt in the idea and decided to aid Macbeth in killing the king so that they may ascend to royalty. Then the king arrives at the castle and is taken care of by Lady Macbeth. She found Macbeth hesitant to kill the king but convinced him to do it. At the end of the night she drugged all the drinks to make sure everyone was asleep. Macbeth then saw a dagger with the hilt facing him in an illusion created by his mind. This emboldened him to go to the king's chambers and kill him. 

The four points we covered in class were the witches’ prophecy, the king's reward to Macbeth, Lady Macbeth's influence and the plan to kill the king. The witches' prophecy haunts the rest of the play, specifically the last line of their introduction fair is foul and foul is fair. They set the theme and mood for the play and foreshadow much of what is to come. The reward given to Macbeth ultimately allows him to grow his ambition to become king and gives him a method to do so because the king wishes to visit his castle. Lady Macbeth's influence especially in Macbeth's time of hesitation was the main factor for Macbeth's decision for power. Lastly the plan to kill the king and the belief it was a part of faith led Macbeth down the wrong path because he gave into ambition and the witches' trick.

1. Macbeth and Banquo were honored because of their great courage in battle. The Thane of Cawdor was sentenced to death, and King Duncan says that Macbeth will be the new Thane. Three witches appear to Macbeth and Banquo, and say that Macbeth will be king and so will Banquo's sons. Macbeth is confused and thinks about how he will take the throne. He is reminded that in order to take the throne, he must have to kill the one who reigns. King Duncan dines at Macbeth's castle, where Macbeth and his wife, Lady Macbeth, decide that they will kill Duncan. Macbeth has second thoughts, but goes through with it.

2. In class, we talked about how fair is foul and foul is fair. This means that there was a reversal of good and evil. In this specific case, Macbeth was honored for his bravery, and he was going to be named Thane of Cawdor. But, after hearing that he may ascend to the throne, he decided to kill the king.

The witches also manipulate Macbeth by providing him with ambiguous prophecies that seem reassuring but they are filling Macbeth's mind with evil intentions. 
We talked about how Lady Macbeth was a good host because she didn't want to give away her scheme to kill the king. She wants to gain his favor before the deed is done, and she has no remorse. However, what we also talked about in class was how Macbeth hesitated because he didn't think that it was right and he thought that the king was highly respected, but Lady Macbeth convinced Macbeth to kill the king.

In Act 1 of Macbeth, the play introduces the main characters and the central conflict. The Three Witches meet after a battle and predict that Macbeth will become Thane of Cawdor and later king. Soon after, Macbeth learns that one of the prophecies has already come true, which makes him start thinking about becoming king. Lady Macbeth reads a letter sent from Macbeth and begins planning how he can take the throne. By the end of Act 1, both Macbeth and Lady Macbeth are thinking about murder as a way to take the throne and fulfill the prophecy. One important point we covered in class was the witches who represent evil and create confusion about fate and free will (also bad=good and good=bad). Another point was Macbeth's ambition, because the prophecies awaken his desire for power even though he knows it is wrong. We also discussed Lady Macbeth's strong and controlling personality (which was unusual for the time), and she pushes Macbeth to act without fear. The fourth and final point was the role of loyalty and honor, since Macbeth is praised as a brave and loyal warrior at the start, which makes his thoughts of betrayal more shocking and shows how quickly ambition can change a person.

1. At the beginning of Act 1 we are introduced to Macdonwald. Macdonwald was a rebel leader who fought against the Scottish King Duncan. Macbeth was able to kill Macdonwald in battle and the rebels fled. As soon as the battle was won Norway tried to attack the weakened scottish forces. The Thane of Cawdor had also betrayed King Duncan and allied himself with the Norwegians. Macbeth and Banquo lead a counter attack against the Norwegians and manage to win. On the way back from the battle three witches stop Macbeth and Banquo. The three witches hail Macbeth by saying he will become the Thane of Cawdor and become king. They then say to Banquo his son's will become king. Before Macbeth and Banquo could ask questions the three witches disapear. Macbeth and Banquo are left to wounder if what they saw and hear was real. A short time later Ross, a nobel man, then informs Macbeth that he has become the Thane of Cawdor because of his actions. After the king lavishes praise on Macbeth he also crowns Malcom as his heir. At the start of the next scene Lady Macbeth recieves a letter from Macbeth. This letter informs Lady Macbeth of the witches prophecy. Lady Macbeth then resolves to do anything to kill King Duncan and gain power. King Duncan then arrives and Lady Macbeth acts as a good host. Macbeth is still doubting whether he should kill King Duncan, but Lady Macbeth mercilessly pressures Macbeth into killing King Duncan.

2. a. The witches are supposed to be seen as different and an inversion of the normal moral view. This is shown by their reversed line beat and being described as not women or men, giving them an inhuman feeling. They also have scenes in which they act awful to people adding to their non human nature. They also start the plot with their evil intentions.

b. Lady Macbeth asks dark spirits to hardner her heart against any sympathies. She asks for them to unsex her, basically turning her heartless and gives her a sense of not being completely human. Yet, she still has enough charm to act as a good hostess and trap King Duncan. Latter when talking with Macbeth she describes her as more of a man than he.

c. Throughout Act 1 Macbeth has a lot of asides, in which he talks to himself about how awful and unatural the idea of kill King Duncan is. He continues to wrestle with it and even almost resolves not to do it. If he where to kill King Duncan it would be doubly as bad because he is the host and he would be going against hospitality as well as murdering another. It takes Lady Macbeth's mercilous emotional manipulation to drive him down the path. 

d. In real history there was a person named Macbeth who killed the King and took power. The King in Shakespeare's time also faced assassination and was very sensitive on the topic. Making the history and story it was based on very risky for Shakespeare. The King during Shakepeare's time launched multiple witch hunts and believed in demonology. Shakespeare also had to include his patrons whishes. At the time there was religious turmoil and Shakespeare attempted to weigh in by asking questions about fate and choice.
